question.prompt: Simplify \(\left(1-\frac{1}{x+1}\right)\div\left(\frac{x}{x^2-1}\right)\), then find its value when \(x=5\).

solutions.explanation: Inside the parentheses, \(1-\frac{1}{x+1}=\frac{x}{x+1}\). Dividing by \(\frac{x}{x^2-1}\) means multiplying by \(\frac{x^2-1}{x}\), giving \((x-1)\). When \(x=5\), its value is \(4\).
solutions.title: Simplify, then substitute
